meta.title: What is DSX
meta.description: DSX is Despia's framework for real native apps. One document per screen, one API on every platform, and a structure AI agents can operate.

meta.title: Quickstart
meta.description: Scaffold a DSX app, run it, change it, check it and build it, in about five minutes.

meta.title: Project structure
meta.description: What each file and folder in a DSX project is for, which ones you write, and which ones the tools generate.

meta.title: Pages and components
meta.description: A .dsx document is one screen or one component, with its markup, its CSS and its logic in a single file.

meta.title: Data and state
meta.description: Variables hold values, formulas derive them, actions change them, and the screen follows. Lists, inputs, APIs and app-wide state work the same way.

meta.title: Styling is CSS
meta.description: The look of a DSX app is standard CSS, in a style attribute, a sheet in the head, or a sheet beside the component. There are no styling attributes.

meta.title: Attributes are data
meta.description: An attribute carries data into an element or a component. The look is always CSS, so every attribute you see means something about the data.

meta.title: Naming rules
meta.description: Markup is kebab-case like HTML, JavaScript and API names are camelCase, CSS is kebab-case, and every name has one spelling.

meta.title: Native UI
meta.description: The elements and components DSX ships, grouped by what they are for, and how each one takes the look of the platform it runs on.

meta.title: Navigation
meta.description: One navigation model on every platform: a route table, a stack of pages, tabs, sheets and deep links. You write the pages; DSX draws the back button.

meta.title: Native features
meta.description: Add a package, then call it from any action as dsx.module.<package>.<action>(). Results, errors, permissions and events work the same for every package.

meta.title: iOS, Android and web
meta.description: One document runs on three platforms. What each one renders today, how a screen adapts to the window, and what is measured rather than claimed.

meta.title: Despia CLI
meta.description: Create, run, check, build and ship a DSX app from the terminal. The commands you use most, grouped by what you are doing.

meta.title: The Despia Console
meta.description: console.despia.com is where your team creates apps, builds them, connects the stores and ships. Everything in it also works from the CLI.

meta.title: Use your AI agent
meta.description: Connect your coding agent to Despia's hosted MCP server and to the CLI's own MCP server, install the agent skills, and give it the checks that keep its changes safe.

meta.title: Agent skills
meta.description: Skills teach a coding agent how to write, structure, review and ship DSX apps. Install the pack once and your agent loads the right one when it needs it.

meta.title: Convert overview
meta.description: Convert puts the web app you already have into a native iOS and Android app, and lets it call native features from its own JavaScript. Available today.

meta.title: Quickstart
meta.description: From your web app's address to a native app on your phone that calls a native feature.

meta.title: V3 web app to V4
meta.description: Move a Despia V3 web app to V4. Your site keeps running, your old despia() calls keep working through the Legacy package, and you move to dsx.module one page at a time.

meta.title: V3 native rebuild
meta.description: Rebuild a V3 app's screens as native DSX screens, one at a time. Not yet available to start from the console.

meta.title: V3 to V4 feature map
meta.description: Every Despia V3 feature and the V4 package or API it moves to, with the gaps marked.

meta.title: What changed since the V4 beta
meta.description: The spellings that were renamed before the first release, and what to use instead. Nothing has been deprecated, because no old spelling has shipped.

meta.title: Web app quickstart
meta.description: Put the React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte or plain JavaScript app you already have inside an iOS and Android app, then call your first native feature from its own code.

meta.title: Calling native features
meta.description: The one form every native call takes, what it returns, how it fails, how to check that a build has a package, and how to listen to events.

meta.title: Frameworks
meta.description: The same dsx.module call in React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte and plain JavaScript. The one rule is where the call runs - in the browser, never on the server.

meta.title: TypeScript
meta.description: Declare the dsx global once, either as any in one line or with a typed declaration for has, on and the error shape.

meta.title: Outside Despia
meta.description: When the same site also runs in normal browsers, write window.dsx?. for the calls that run in both places. This is the only page where that form appears.

meta.title: Hosted or bundled
meta.description: The app either loads your site from its address, or ships your static build inside the app and serves it from a local origin. When to use which, and how your dev server fits in.

meta.title: Preview and test
meta.description: Try your native calls in a browser with despia dev, where the browser answers what it can and simulates the rest, then run the real app on a simulator or your phone.

meta.title: Package index
meta.description: Every native feature your web app can call today, with its lead call. Each links to the package's one sample and its full reference.

meta.title: Minimum functionality
meta.description: The app has to be more than a website or a brochure in an app shell: real navigation, real depth, and features people expect from an app in its category. Reviewers judge perceived value, not the technology.

meta.title: Website-style design
meta.description: The app must look and behave like an app on the device: a title bar, bottom tabs or a navigation stack, touch-sized controls. Reviewers often cite this together with 4.2 as "a repackaged website".

meta.title: In-app purchase
meta.description: Digital goods and services sold inside the app go through Apple's in-app purchase (and Google Play Billing on Android), with a working restore, and products that are configured and purchasable.

meta.title: Subscriptions and paywalls
meta.description: A paywall must state what is bought, the price and billing period, and the trial terms clearly, be easy to dismiss, and never trick the user into a purchase.

meta.title: Privacy policy
meta.description: Every app that collects or shares data needs a reachable privacy policy, linked in the store listing and inside the app, that matches what the app and its SDKs actually do.

meta.title: Data minimization
meta.description: Only ask for personal data the app's features need; anything optional must be clearly optional and explained.

meta.title: App Tracking Transparency
meta.description: Tracking a user across other companies' apps and websites needs the App Tracking Transparency prompt first, the choice must be respected, and the App Store privacy labels must match.

meta.title: AI data sharing
meta.description: Before personal data is sent to a third-party AI service, the app must say so clearly and get the user's permission.

meta.title: Login services
meta.description: An app that offers third-party or social login (Google, Facebook and so on) must also offer an equivalent login option that meets Apple's privacy requirements; Sign in with Apple is the usual answer.

meta.title: Blank screens during login
meta.description: Reviewers reject flows that show blank or white screens or look unresponsive, which often happens during an OAuth redirect.

meta.title: Spam and copies
meta.description: Apps that duplicate others already on the store, or that ship many near-identical variants, are rejected.

meta.title: Accurate metadata
meta.description: The name, description, screenshots and previews must show the app as it is, without features it does not have or misleading claims.

meta.title: Account deletion
meta.description: An app that lets people create an account must also let them start deleting that account from inside the app.
